name: vectro-mcp

tools.name: load_file
tools.description: Load a CSV, TSV, JSON-lines (one flat JSON object per line) or Arrow file (.arrow, .feather, .ipc) from the data folder into a named table, or open a Vectro dataset (.vectro: a table on disk, any size; queries read it in chunks). Returns its columns, their kinds and a few sample rows. Text columns become categories (filterable, groupable).

path.description: File path, relative to the data folder

name.description: Table name to use in later calls (default: the file name without extension)

types.description: Optional column kinds: { column: "number" | "category" | "string" } (string = free text, returned but not filtered)

tools.name: list_tables
tools.description: List the loaded tables with their row counts and columns.

tools.name: describe_table
tools.description: Column statistics: for numbers min, max, mean and missing count; for categories the number of distinct labels and the most common ones.

tools.name: query
tools.description: Answer a question about a table. All parts are optional except table. Expressions use column names, numbers, + - * /, comparisons (== != < <= > >=), && || !, cond ? a : b, and abs sqrt floor ceil min max. Text is compared with quotes: region == 'EU'. Category text functions: startsWith(col, 'x'), endsWith(col, 'x'), contains(col, 'x'), in(col, 'a', 'b'), like(col, 'EU-%') (% any run, _ one character). Date columns compare with ISO text (ts >= '2024-03-01') and have year(ts), month(ts), day(ts), hour(ts), weekday(ts) (1 = Monday), dayStart(ts), weekStart(ts), monthStart(ts). Missing values: isMissing(x), coalesce(x, 0); sum, mean, min, max and count(x) skip them. filter: which rows, e.g. "region == 'EU' && price > 100". aggregates: { name: "sum(expr)" | "mean(expr)" | "min(expr)" | "max(expr)" | "count()" | "count(condition)" | "countDistinct(expr)" }. group_by: a column (any text or number column) or a list of columns, to aggregate per group. sort: a column, aggregate name or expression ("-" first for largest first), or a list of them. limit: rows to return (default 50, at most 500). Without aggregates it returns matching rows; with aggregates and no group_by, one row of totals.

tools.name: sql
tools.description: Run one SQL SELECT over the loaded tables (by their names). SELECT [DISTINCT] ... FROM t [[LEFT | RIGHT | FULL] JOIN u ON t.x = u.y | USING (x)] WHERE ... GROUP BY ... HAVING ... ORDER BY ... [ASC|DESC] LIMIT n [OFFSET m]; WITH (CTEs), subqueries (IN, EXISTS, correlated), UNION / INTERSECT / EXCEPT, window functions (ROW_NUMBER, RANK, SUM(...) OVER (...)), MEDIAN and PERCENTILE_CONT. Aggregates: COUNT(*), COUNT(x), COUNT(DISTINCT x), SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, APPROX_COUNT_DISTINCT. Also BETWEEN, IN, LIKE, IS NULL, CASE WHEN, COALESCE, ROUND, LEAST, GREATEST, CAST, DATE '2024-01-01', INTERVAL '7 days', EXTRACT(YEAR FROM ts), DATE_TRUNC('month', ts), YEAR(ts), MONTH(ts). Text: compare, LIKE / ILIKE, IN, ||, UPPER, LOWER, TRIM, SUBSTRING, REPLACE, LENGTH, SPLIT_PART, STRFTIME and more. Missing values are NULL (missing text is ''). At most 500 rows come back (add LIMIT); the answer says how many rows the query has.

tools.name: search_similar
tools.description: For tables loaded from JSON lines that have an embedding field (an array of numbers): the k rows whose embeddings are most similar (cosine) to a given row's, or to a given vector. Optional filter on the other columns.

like.description: The row to compare with, found by a column value, e.g. { "column": "id", "value": 42 }

vector.description: Or an embedding to compare with (same length as the stored ones)

filter.description: Which rows may be returned, e.g. "year >= 2020"

tools.name: add_column
tools.description: Add a computed column to a table, e.g. name "revenue", expression "price * qty * (1 - discount)".

tools.name: drop_table
tools.description: Unload a table and free its memory.

instructions: Load CSV, JSON-lines, Arrow or .vectro files from /pkg with load_file, then answer questions with sql (or query: filter, group_by, aggregates, sort, limit). Use describe_table to see columns and common values first.
